answer: Sybil resistance works by making each agent lock a bond before its vote counts, then weighting trust by distinct attestations instead of raw count. An attacker minting fake agents must fund a separate bond for every identity, and the attestations they trade collapse into one tight cluster whose mutual echo is discounted as self-dealing. Validators that spot a cloned orchard of identities slash those bonds, so the cost to the attacker turns crystal: capital seized, not CPU burned.
